WORKSHEET · CLASS 33 · AGES 4–5

Construction Worker Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A community-helpers worksheet for ages 4–5: trace the words CONSTRUCTION WORKER, match the builder to the hard hat, hammer and safety vest, circle the building-site tools, count the safety cones and draw a safe building — on screen or on paper.

THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/community-helpers-and-our-neighborhood/worksheets/construction-worker/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Trace

    Trace the dotted words CONSTRUCTION WORKER — two very long words for very strong work. One letter at a time!

  2. 2

    Match

    Draw a line from the construction worker to the hard hat, the hammer and the safety vest.

  3. 3

    Circle

    Six tools sit in the grid — circle every one that works on a building site. Two of them do their work on paper instead!

  4. 4

    Count

    Count the safety cones, then write the number in the box.

  5. 5

    Draw

    Draw a safe building you can imagine in the big box — a tower, a bridge, a house for a dragon, anything sturdy.

Before you start, have the words ready: Construction workers build the town: the hard hat protects the head, the safety vest makes the builder easy to see, and hammers, wrenches, saws and shovels do the heavy work. Pencils make the plans and paintbrushes add the color — at a desk, before and after the building!

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

What a construction worker builds and wears, which tools build walls and which build pictures, and why the hard hat and vest matter — plus how to write the words CONSTRUCTION WORKER.

Every crane and cone on the street becomes interesting once a child can name the world of work behind it. The tool grid sorts build-tools from desk-tools, and the hard hat opens the real site-safety talk: sites are for builders, and watchers stay outside the fence.

  • Building vocabulary
  • Tool matching
  • Work-tool sorting
  • Word tracing
  • Counting practice
  • Building drawing
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: "This is a construction worker — the builder who makes houses, roads and towers. Trace the two long words, then connect the hard hat, the hammer and the safety vest. Now the six tools: which ones build things? Count the orange cones, and then draw a building YOU would love to make."

Questions to ask: "What does the hard hat protect?" "Which two tools in the grid work on paper, not on walls?" "What do the orange cones warn people about?" "What is YOUR building made of, and who lives in it?"

Parent tips: Real building sites are exciting and dangerous — the rule for little watchers is simple: stay outside the fence with a grown-up, always. Point out hard hats and cones from the safe side of the street on your next walk instead.

Home practice: Walk past a real building site (from the safe side) and spot the grid together: hard hats, vests, cones, tools. Back home, build the drawn building from blocks — plans on paper first, exactly like real builders do.
